notes:
Git, and links to your files and folders, like the ones Claude Code has.

- **A git tool.** In a chat with Tasks on, she uses git in your allowed folders with its own tool instead of typing git commands. Reading never asks: status, diffs, the log, a commit, blame, branches and the stash list. A commit, a new branch, switching branch, and stashing or unstashing show you a card first (the message and the files for a commit), and you choose Run or Skip. A commit, a new branch and a switch have **Undo** on their card. Undo turns a commit back into staged changes, and it refuses once something has changed since.
- **Push and pull ask too.** A push asks even with asking off, because it sends your work out. With skip permissions on, a push or pull asks unless the remote is on your own network. Nothing is ever forced: no force-push, no amend, no hard reset, no skipping hooks, and a pull only fast-forwards. If git refuses, she tells you what it said.
- **Your projects, for reading.** An app built on Serenity can list repositories she may read (the Serenity Framework's Projects). In a chat with an agent you've let look at that place, she can read them by name, with or without Tasks, but never change them. Changing a repository needs its folder under Settings → Tasks.
- **Careful with what a repository says.** Reading turns off the settings in a repository that could start a program (an fsmonitor, external diff tools), and nothing she names can be read as an option. What git shows her is treated as content, never instructions, like a file she reads. If git isn't installed, she says so and points to git-scm.com.
- **Links to files and folders.** A path in her message, or in one of her docs, becomes a link when it's a real file or folder on this computer. Click it to see it selected in Explorer (your file manager on Linux). The small **↗** beside it opens it in its usual app. Programs, scripts and shortcuts are only ever shown, never opened. Serenity's own data folder and network paths (`\\server\share`) never become links, so a message can't send your Windows sign-in to another computer. A path with spaces needs to be in `backticks` to be found.
